title.narrative: Horticulture Market Acceleration Program-HortiMAP

description.narrative: HortiMAP is a four-year project designed to support the horticulture sector to become Modern, resilient, and sustainable while creating jobs, increasing incomes and nutrition outcomes for women, men, and youth; the project is premised on three objectives: 1) improving the productivity and supply of high-quality horticulture products; 2) improving competitiveness and access to markets; and 3) strengthening relevant regulatory frameworks. The project is pursuing these objectives by improving the skills and capacities of farmers, providing access to finance across a broader spectrum of value chain stakeholders, providing technical assistance to improve identified areas of weakness, creating awareness of different quality requirements, improving the quality of production, and increasing access to premium markets. It is also working with the regulatory bodies to ensure that the existing standards are known to stakeholders, supporting the enforcement of standards, improving access to institutional services, and facilitating the development of certification standards.

title.narrative: Ugandan consumers have increased awareness of FFV safety/quality concerns

description.narrative: Consumers are reached with information that structurally and/or systemically contributes to improving their nutritional situation, as a result of being aware of the benefits consuming fruits and vegetables (FFV). This result therefore is of the level to which the consumers are aware of the benefits of consuming fresh fruits and vegetables, with the aim of ensuring they act on actually buying more fruits and vegetables and consuming them approprietly in the recommended portions. This information to be aware of covers the multiple dimensions of food security, in relation to relaying the benefits of consuming FFV (availability, access, utilization, stability). The consumers are reached with this information through multiple fora such as through the consumer reach initiatives of the market vendors, through food safety campaigns and through radio talk shows, all facilitated by the project

title.narrative: Service provision capacity of the horticultural public sector is strengthened

description.narrative: Key public sector actors capacity is to be built, to ensure that they offer a condusive regulatory and policy environment for fruit and vegetable market actors, at all levels of the value chain. In addition, these public sector actors are to offer effective and efficient services to these sector market actors accordingly. The targeted public sector actors in this case include the Ministry of Agriculture, Animal Industry and Fisheries (MAAIF), Ministry of Trade, Industry and Cooperatives (MTIC), National Agricultural Research Organization (NARO), Uganda National Bureau of Standards (UNBS), Uganda Export Promotion Board (UEPB) and the various District Local Governments and City Councils where the project works.
